newsitem.title: CHINA: Templeton buys floor of Shanghai stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Templeton buys floor of Shanghai stock exchange.

text.p: One of the largest U.S. mutual fund companies, Templeton Emerging Markets Fund Inc, on Tuesday bought a floor in the new Shanghai stock exchange building, a building official said.

The building, shaped like a huge square arch and jointly developed by the stock exchange and the People's Liberation Army, is situated in the new Pudong development zone east of Shanghai's city centre.
The official said Templeton paid more than $3 million to buy a floor with a total area of 1,240 square meters (13,342 square feet), an average of $2,419 per square metre.
The stock exchange, currently located in an old building in the centre of the city, is scheduled to start partial operations in the new building on July 1.
The Shanghai Securities News quoted Templeton president Mark Mobius as saying the offices would be used as the headquarters of the company's Southeast Asian operations.

"Shanghai will be China's financial centre and the Shanghai Stock Exchange will be the most important bourse in Southeast Asia," Mark Mobius said. "That's why we decided to set up our future Southeast Asian headquarters here."
Brokers said they expected Templeton to be among the first foreign companies to receive a mutual fund licence in China when Beijing opens up the industry.
Regulations governing mutual fund investment are being drawn up and are expected to be released later this year.
Templeton Emerging Markets Fund Inc is a subsidiary of Franklin Resources Inc, which manages funds in excess of US$150 billion.
